sources.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zurich 2024 FS complete lecture script, 176 pages
sources.locator: Complete 176-page author-hosted lecture script retrieved. Read Chapter 13, §13.2, printed pp. 13.3–13.9 (PDF pp. 154–160), for the cross-sectional eigenvalue problem, propagation cutoff, real longitudinal wave numbers, and evanescent decay. No open-end scattering existence result is claimed from this section.

contents.name: §13.2: fixed-frequency propagating and evanescent mode branches
contents.support: The source supports the guide-mode and cutoff terminology in its stated rectangular lossless guide class. The local definition treats the finite channel list and unique port map as explicit interface inputs, not as consequences of this theorem.

contents.name: §13.2: only finitely many modes propagate at a fixed frequency in the declared guide class
contents.support: This is used only as model context; the item does not generalize completeness or finite-channel well-posedness to arbitrary device geometries.

sources.title: Weng Cho Chew, Theory of Microwave and Optical Waveguides, Purdue lecture notes, complete 362-page text
sources.locator: Complete 362-page lecture text retrieved. Read §1.6.1 (printed p. 10/PDF p. 19), §§1.7.1–1.7.4 (printed pp. 10–12/PDF pp. 19–22), §1.12.2 (printed pp. 25–26/PDF pp. 34–35), §2.4 (printed pp. 50–52/PDF pp. 60–61), and §§5.1–5.2.2 (PDF pp. 188–198). The notes use e^{+jωt}; local items use e^{-iωt}.

contents.name: §1.6.1: source-free Lorentz boundary identity for transpose-symmetric constitutive tensors
contents.support: This is independent reciprocity context. The local theorem states its exact C1 and transpose-symmetry hypotheses and derives the matrix identity from its own port pairing.

contents.name: §§1.7.1–1.7.4: time/frequency Poynting identities and time-average power
contents.support: The source distinguishes the time-domain energy law from the frequency-domain complex-power identity. The local proof derives the finite Lorentz/Drude loss balance from the actual adopted postulates.

contents.name: §1.12.2: incident and reflected channel vectors related by a scattering matrix
contents.support: This supports the standard map notation. The local definition adds SI power units, regularity, channel completeness assumptions, and an explicit well-posedness boundary.

contents.name: §2.4: modal power flow in a lossless propagating guide mode
contents.support: This supports power normalization at a reference port; the local item stipulates the complete flux-orthogonal channel pairing directly.

contents.name: §§5.2.1–5.2.2: junction matching uses infinitely many modes; higher-order evanescent modes are localized near the junction
contents.support: The local definition retains evanescent modes in exact matching and explicitly excludes any claim that a finite truncation of them is exact.

contents.name: §§5.2.1–5.2.2: finite truncations are computational approximations to infinite matching systems
contents.support: The local finite S matrix indexes propagating channels only; it does not replace the near-junction matching system by a finite evanescent-mode truncation.

sources.title: Roger B. Marks and Dylan F. Williams, A General Waveguide Circuit Theory, Journal of Research of the National Institute of Standards and Technology 97(5) (1992), pp. 533–562
sources.locator: Complete 30-page NIST-hosted article retrieved. Read §5, printed pp. 555–556 (PDF pp. 22–23), and Appendix D, printed pp. 559–560 (PDF pp. 26–27), including the corrected reciprocity relation for power waves.

contents.name: §5: power-wave amplitudes and the net-power relation
contents.support: The source distinguishes power waves from traveling waves when the characteristic impedance is complex. The local definition therefore states its channel flux normalization as a model condition.

contents.name: §5 and Appendix D: reciprocal power-wave scattering matrices need not be symmetric for lossy waveguides
contents.support: This is a scope warning retained in the item: symmetry is proved only for bases satisfying the exact Lorentz bilinear port pairing, not from power normalization alone.

contents.name: §5: total port power is associated with the full channel vector
contents.support: The local matrix example distinguishes the full two-channel output from the one-channel projection observed by a reduced model.

contents.name: §1.12.2: scattering-matrix channel representation and lossless unitary consequence

contents.name: §1.12.2: incident-to-outgoing vector relation
contents.support: The local example computes the two-channel unitary swap and the one-channel projected matrix directly.
